headline: Teacher's 30-Year Vision: Minnesota Wetlands Come Back to Life

summary_short: A retired biology teacher has spent over 30 years transforming his Minnesota property back to its natural state, turning ditches into wetlands and pasture into oak savan…
body:
For more than three decades, Mike Niziolek, a former AP biology teacher, has methodically restored his 150-acre property near Elk River, Minnesota, returning it to the landscape it resembled hundreds of years ago. Wetlands that once thrived on the land are now coming back to life, drawing wildlife to what Niziolek calls "bio supermarkets"—ecosystems rich enough to sustain diverse species.

The transformation has been gradual and deliberate. Niziolek converted pastered land into oak savanna, reclaimed tilled soil as prairie, and restored ditched areas to functioning wetlands. The Minnesota Land Trust recognized his decades of stewardship in 2018, awarding him Landowner of the Year. By 2024, when media outlets spoke with him about his work, the property had become a testament to what patience and ecological knowledge can achieve on a single plot of land.
